evidence: `fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py` uses multiple incompatible error channels: `find_plan()` returns `(None, "error string")` on failures (lines 147, 152, 160, 163), `get_project_name()` swallows subprocess failures and silently falls back (lines 46-51), and `main()` sometimes prints stderr + exits (lines 224-229).

`fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py` has format-dependent failure semantics for empty results: text mode exits non-zero for `--list` with no plans (lines 209-211), while JSON mode emits `[]` and exits 0 (lines 201-208, 220).

`fando-verify/scripts/find_plan.py` does not guard `base_dir.iterdir()` when the plan root is missing (line 113), so one code path raises an uncaught exception while adjacent paths return controlled errors.

`fando-verify/scripts/parse_verification.py` mixes parse errors and domain verdicts into the same process-exit channel: parse failure exits 1 (lines 184-189), and valid parse with regressions/missing also exits 1 (lines 215-217), while JSON responses may include `warning` on successful parse (lines 206-208).

findings.summary: Related scripts encode failures with different contracts, making callers branch on ad-hoc behavior.
evidence: `parse_verification()` uses `VerificationResult.error` plus partial-success states, and `main()` conditionally maps those to stderr/json/exit code (parse_verification.py lines 184-189, 206-208, 215-217).
This creates two incompatible error interfaces for neighboring CLI utilities that are both consumed as automation helpers.
findings.suggestion: Define one shared script error contract (for example: `{ok, error_code, message, data}` in JSON plus aligned exit-code policy) and apply it in both scripts. Refactor `find_plan.py` to return structured results instead of `(None, str)` and align `parse_verification.py` warnings/errors to the same schema.

findings.summary: In `find_plan.py`, identical no-data conditions fail in text mode but succeed in JSON mode.
evidence: For `--list` with no plans, text mode prints "No plans found." and exits 1 (find_plan.py lines 209-211).
The same condition in JSON mode emits an empty list and exits 0 (find_plan.py lines 201-208, 220).
Sibling script `parse_verification.py` does not vary error exit semantics by output format for empty stdin (parse_verification.py lines 178-180), showing internal inconsistency in CLI error policy.
findings.suggestion: Make exit behavior independent of presentation format: either treat empty list as success in both modes, or treat it as error in both. Document the rule and enforce it consistently across both scripts.

findings.summary: Plan listing has an unhandled filesystem boundary that bypasses scripted error handling.
evidence: `list_plans()` calls `base_dir.iterdir()` without existence/IO guards (find_plan.py line 113), which can raise when `~/.claude/plan-reviews` is absent or inaccessible.
Other paths in the same script return controlled errors instead of throwing (find_plan.py lines 72-73, 147, 152, 160, 163), so this path is a behavioral outlier.
`parse_verification.py` consistently converts boundary failures (empty stdin / parse failure) to explicit messages and exit codes (lines 178-180, 184-189), highlighting mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit handling for missing/unreadable review directories in `list_plans()` and map to the same structured failure channel used elsewhere (and in `parse_verification.py`).
